title_en: Regulations for the Implementation of the Environmental Protection Tax Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Environmental Protection Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Environmental Protection Tax Law).

Article 2 The specific scope of other solid wastes referred to in the Tax Items and Tax Amounts Table of Environmental Protection Tax attached to the Environmental Protection Tax Law shall be determined in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Paragraph 2 of Article 6 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law.

Article 3 The centralized urban and rural sewage treatment sites specified in Article 5, Paragraph 1 and Article 12, Paragraph 1, Item 3 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law refer to sites that provide domestic sewage treatment services to the public, excluding sites that provide sewage treatment services to enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators within industrial parks, development zones, and other industrial agglomeration areas, as well as sewage treatment sites self-built and self-used by enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators.

Article 4 Livestock and poultry farms that meet the scale standards determined by the provincial people's government and have pollutant discharge outlets shall pay environmental protection tax according to law; if comprehensive utilization and harmless treatment of livestock and poultry breeding waste are carried out according to law, such treatment shall not be deemed as directly discharging pollutants to the environment, and no environmental protection tax shall be paid.

Article 5 The tax basis for taxable solid wastes shall be determined based on the discharge amount of solid wastes. The discharge amount of solid wastes shall be the balance of the generation amount of taxable solid wastes in the current period minus the storage amount, disposal amount, and comprehensive utilization amount of taxable solid wastes in the current period.
The storage amount and disposal amount of solid wastes as mentioned in the preceding paragraph refer to the amount of solid wastes stored or disposed of in facilities or sites that meet the national and local environmental protection standards; the comprehensive utilization amount of solid wastes refers to the amount of solid wastes comprehensively utilized in accordance with the requirements of the development and reform, industry and information technology departments of the State Council on resource comprehensive utilization and the national and local environmental protection standards.

Article 8 Where taxable pollutants are discharged from two or more discharge outlets, the environmental protection tax shall be calculated and levied separately for the taxable pollutants discharged from each discharge outlet; if the taxpayer holds a pollutant discharge permit, the pollutant discharge outlets shall be determined according to the pollutant discharge outlets specified in the pollutant discharge permit.

Article 9 For taxpayers falling under the circumstances specified in Item 2 of Article 10 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law, if the monitoring data obtained by the taxpayer's own monitoring of pollutants comply with the relevant national provisions and monitoring specifications, such data shall be deemed as monitoring data issued by the monitoring institutions specified in Item 2 of Article 10 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law.

Article 10 The concentration value of taxable air pollutants or water pollutants referred to in Article 13 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law means the numerical value obtained by averaging the hourly average concentrations of taxable air pollutants automatically monitored by the automatic pollutant monitoring equipment installed and used by the taxpayer in the current month, or the numerical value obtained by averaging the daily average concentrations of taxable water pollutants, or the average of the concentrations of taxable air pollutants or water pollutants monitored by the monitoring institution in the current month.
Where environmental protection tax is reduced in accordance with Article 13 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law, the hourly average concentration of taxable air pollutants or the daily average concentration of taxable water pollutants as specified in the preceding paragraph, as well as the concentration of taxable air pollutants or water pollutants monitored each time by the monitoring institution in the current month, shall not exceed the pollutant discharge standards prescribed by the state and the local authorities.

For taxpayers that reduce their environmental protection tax in accordance with Article 13 of the Environmental Protection Tax Law, they shall calculate separately for different taxable pollutants discharged from each discharge outlet.

The tax authorities shall, according to law, perform duties such as accepting environmental protection tax declaration, comparing tax-related information, and organizing tax payment into the state treasury.
The competent department of environmental protection shall, according to law, be responsible for the monitoring and management of taxable pollutants and formulate and improve pollutant monitoring norms.

Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen leadership over the collection and management of environmental protection tax, and promptly coordinate and resolve major issues in the collection and management of environmental protection tax.

The tax and environmental protection competent departments of the State Council shall formulate technical standards for the tax-related information sharing platform and norms for data collection, storage, transmission, query, and use.

Where taxpayers discharge taxable pollutants across regions, and the tax authorities have disputes over the jurisdiction of tax collection, the disputing parties shall negotiate and resolve the matter in accordance with the principle of facilitating collection and management; if they fail to reach a consensus through negotiation, they shall report to the common higher-level tax authority for a decision.

The tax authorities shall identify taxpayers based on the information of pollutant discharging entities delivered by the competent department of environmental protection.
For taxpayers for which there is no corresponding information in the information on pollutant discharging entities delivered by the competent department of environmental protection, the tax authorities shall identify them when the taxpayers handle the environmental protection tax declaration for the first time, and deliver the relevant information to the competent department of environmental protection.

If the competent department of environmental protection discovers errors in the information on taxable pollutant discharge declared by the taxpayer or in the applicable pollutant discharge coefficient or material balance calculation method, it shall notify the tax authorities to handle the matter.

Article 21 Where the pollutant emission data declared by a taxpayer is inconsistent with the relevant data submitted by the competent department of environmental protection, the tax basis for taxable pollutants shall be determined in accordance with the data submitted by the competent department of environmental protection.

Article 23 Tax authorities and competent departments of environmental protection shall, free of charge, provide taxpayers with guidance, training, and consulting services related to the payment of environmental protection tax.
Article 24 Tax authorities shall carry out tax inspection on environmental protection tax according to law, and competent departments of environmental protection shall cooperate.
Article 25 Taxpayers shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions on tax collection administration, properly keep the relevant materials on the monitoring and management of taxable pollutants.

Article 26 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2018. The Regulations on the Levy and Use of Pollutant Discharge Fees promulgated by the State Council on January 2, 2003 shall be abolished simultaneously.
